```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5)
has_plots <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)
```

`pelagicOM` builds a completely known **operating truth** for testing CPUE
standardisation methods. It has two parts, run one after the other:

1. **Biomass (Part I)**: total biomass $B_{total}(y)$ from a
   Pella-Tomlinson model with an exogenous removal rate, distributed over a
   1x1 degree grid as $B(y,s) = B_{total}(y)\,p(y,s)$. The weights
   $p(y,s)$ come from a static habitat (latitudinal envelope, hotspots,
   gradient, persistent Gaussian random field), a redistribution of the
   envelope in time and spatio-temporal AR(1) noise.
2. **Fishery (Part II)**: set-by-set pelagic longline operations on top of
   the biomass truth. It covers fleets, vessels with careers, trips and
   sets, location by preferential sampling and fidelity, latent fishing
   strategies, hooks and hooks between floats (HBF), the components of log
   catchability, Tweedie catches and companion species. Observation
   profiles and scenario data sets are generated from the result.

The `"BET_ICCAT"` preset is the bigeye tuna operating model of Experimento 02
and reproduces its results bit for bit.

```{r}
library(pelagicOM)
om_presets()[, c("preset", "species", "area")]
```

## 1. Biomass truth

```{r}
bcfg <- om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT")
bcfg
sim <- simulate_biomass(bcfg, verbose = FALSE)
sim
head(regional_summary(sim), 3)
```

```{r, eval = has_plots}
fig_total_biomass(sim)
fig_region_share(sim)
```

## 2. Fishery truth and scenario data sets

The full BET fishery has about 1.1 million sets and takes around 15 s.
Here the fleets are reduced to keep the vignette fast:

```{r}
fcfg <- om_fishery_config("BET_ICCAT",
    fleets = list(A = list(n_vessels = 6), B = list(n_vessels = 6),
                  C = list(n_vessels = 5), D = list(n_vessels = 5),
                  E = list(n_vessels = 4)))
fish <- simulate_fishery(sim, fcfg, verbose = FALSE)
fish
scen <- generate_scenarios(fish, verbose = FALSE)
scen
```

The true data keep every latent variable (true strategy, density,
catchability components, expected catch). The scenario data sets keep only
what a real logbook would contain:

```{r}
fish$latent_columns[1:10]
names(scen$datasets[["04_global_temporal_uncertainty"]])
```

```{r, eval = has_plots, fig.height = 6}
fig_cpue_vs_biomass(fish)
```

## 3. Tuning the operating model

Every parameter is in the two configuration lists. `om_config_update()`
(or the `...` of the configuration functions) merges named lists level by
level. Vectors and unnamed lists, such as hotspots or scenarios, are
replaced as a whole, and `NULL` removes an element.

```{r}
cfg_fast <- om_config_update(bcfg,
    population = list(r = 0.45, decline = list(u_peak = 0.35)),
    shift = list(enabled = FALSE))
c(cfg_fast$population$r, cfg_fast$population$decline$u_peak)
```

### An alternative hypothesis for BET

Below, BET follows a different hypothesis:

* The tropical band is split at the equator, giving four regions.
* The envelope widens only to the north, and its centre drifts 3 degrees
  north.
* Fleet E leaves the fishery, and a new fleet F, created with `om_fleet()`,
  enters in 1990 in the southern tropics.

```{r}
dom4 <- om_domain_iccat("BET-A", region_breaks = c(-20, 0, 20),
                        region_labels = c("NORTH", "TROP_N", "TROP_S", "SOUTH"),
                        geometry = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
alt <- om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT",
    shift = list(north_expansion = 1.0, south_expansion = 0,
                 center_drift = 3, ramp = "logistic"))
sim_alt <- simulate_biomass(alt, dom4, long_table = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
reg <- regional_summary(sim_alt)
reg[reg$Year %in% c(1950, 2025), c("Year", "Region", "Share")]
```

The fleets, regional effects and scenarios then follow the new regions
(fleets reduced here to keep the vignette fast):

```{r}
fcfg_alt <- om_fishery_config("BET_ICCAT",
    fleets = list(A = list(n_vessels = 6, regions = c("NORTH", "TROP_N")),
                  B = list(n_vessels = 6, regions = c("NORTH", "TROP_N")),
                  C = list(n_vessels = 5, regions = c("NORTH", "TROP_N")),
                  D = list(n_vessels = 5,
                           regions = c("TROP_N", "TROP_S", "SOUTH")),
                  E = NULL),
    catchability = list(region_effect = c(NORTH = 0, TROP_N = 0,
                                          TROP_S = 0, SOUTH = 0)))
fcfg_alt$fleets$F <- om_fleet(n_vessels = 5, year_start = 1990,
                              regions = c("TROP_S", "SOUTH"),
                              core_lon = -5, core_lat = -10)
fcfg_alt$scenarios <- list(
    list(name = "01_global_complete",
         regions = c("NORTH", "TROP_N", "TROP_S", "SOUTH"),
         drop = character(0), observation = "complete",
         objective = "Reference"),
    list(name = "02_north_temporal", regions = "NORTH",
         drop = character(0), observation = "temporal",
         objective = "Northern region with degraded early data"))
fish_alt <- simulate_fishery(sim_alt, fcfg_alt, verbose = FALSE)
generate_scenarios(fish_alt, verbose = FALSE)
```

Other entry points for tuning:

* `habitat$custom_effect = function(cells) ...` adds any static log-scale
  layer (for example a covariate) to the habitat;
* `population$model` accepts a function `f(B, K, r, shape)`;
* `population$events` adds abrupt shocks to the total biomass;
* `om_domain_iccat()` gives the cells of any ICCAT stock area
  (`iccat_stocks()`), `om_domain_grid()` builds a synthetic domain (for
  example an idealised Atlantic without coastline), and
  `om_domain_from_gpkg()` reads any ICCAT-like GeoPackage.

## 4. Writing the outputs and reproducing Experimento 02

`om_run()` runs everything. When `dir` is given, it writes the files with
the folder structure and names of Experimento 02:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run <- om_run("BET_ICCAT", dir = "Experimento_pelagicOM")
#> Experimento_pelagicOM/Simulacao_Biomassa/outputs/data/biomass_true_base.rds
#> Experimento_pelagicOM/Simulacao_Pesca/outputs/truth/TRUE_FISHERY_DATA_base.rds
#> Experimento_pelagicOM/Simulacao_Pesca/outputs/datasets/01_global_complete.rds
#> ...
om_compare_reference(run, "R-Work/Experimento_02")
```

`om_compare_reference()` compares the biomass, the long table, the fishery
truth and the eight scenario data sets with the reference files and reports
whether each one is `identical()`. The script
`system.file("scripts", "reproduce_experimento02.R", package = "pelagicOM")`
runs the whole proof from the command line.

## Where to go next

The website articles describe each part of the model in detail:

* [Spatial domain](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/spatial-domain.html):
  ICCAT grid, stock areas, regions, GeoPackages, synthetic grids.
* [Part I: biomass](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/biomass.html)
  and [Part II: fishery](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/fishery.html).
* [Observation and scenarios](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/observation-scenarios.html).
* [Tuning](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/tuning.html),
  [outputs](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/outputs.html)
  and the [configuration reference](https://rodrigosantana.github.io/pelagicOM/articles/configuration-reference.html).
